root_cause_label: Incorrect TF Checkpoint Parsing Produces Garbage Weights
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent assumed TensorFlow checkpoint data could be extracted by seeking to arbitrary byte offsets without understanding the actual protobuf-structured binary format, so all weight reads produced garbage and every generated output was degenerate, with the agent cycling through heuristic offset guesses until submission.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 writes the first implementation using `fseek(f,1000000,0)` as a hardcoded arbitrary offset into the binary checkpoint file, acting on the false premise that the TF .ckpt data can be read sequentially from a guessed byte position rather than via proper protobuf tensor-index parsing.
t_commit_evidence: Step 5 commits the entire approach of reading raw float data from arbitrary byte offsets in the checkpoint; all subsequent iterations (steps 7, 9, 11, 16, 19, 22, 26, 29) only vary the offset heuristic (sz/2, sz-total, 50M, 100M, random scan) but never address the fundamental binary format misunderstanding, locking in the failure from the start.
t_surface_evidence: Step 13 is the first test run; the output is `Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ Ġ` (20 repetitive space tokens), a clear observable signal that the weight loading is completely wrong.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified false assumption that the TensorFlow GPT-2 checkpoint binary data could be extracted by seeking to an arbitrary byte offset (e.g., 1,000,000 bytes from the start) and reading raw floats sequentially. In reality, TF checkpoints use a protobuf-encoded index file referencing tensor names, shapes, and byte offsets within sharded data files; naive seeking produces garbage bytes rather than actual weight tensors. The agent never investigated the actual binary structure (the hexdump attempt at step 14 failed and no alternative inspection was tried), so this false premise persisted throughout all 32 steps.
